request.spec:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A steward can assign a REVIEW claim to a user (an entry and a button on the claim;
REVIEW_ASSIGNED naming the claim and ending user=<user>; a blank user, any other status or anyone
else is refused). The claim shows the assigned user, and the header shows the signed-in user the
count of REVIEW claims assigned to them.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A steward can now assign a claim in REVIEW to a user, and the latest `bin/e2e` run passes all 4 tests.

On the first full run, "scenario 1" failed at a claim edit (amount 7.77). The test expected the edit to go through, but the app showed an error. That step doesn't touch anything I changed. The same test passed when run alone, and then passed in two full runs after that. So it looks like a timing flake, but I didn't find out why the edit was refused that one time.

**What changed**
- **Stored data:** a new migration, `V116__claim_review_assigned.sql`, adds a `review_assigned` column to claims. The `Claim` entity keeps the value, and it is copied when a claim is transferred or cloned.
- **Server:** a new endpoint, `POST /api/sheets/{sheet}/claims/{id}/assign-review`, calls `ClaimService.assignReview`. It refuses:
  - a blank user (400)
  - anyone who isn't a steward (403)
  - a claim that isn't in REVIEW (409)

  When it succeeds it writes `REVIEW_ASSIGNED … person= amount= date= user=<user>` to the audit file. If a delegate makes the assignment, the existing audit service adds `for=<steward>` on its own. Claims sent to the browser now include `reviewAssigned`.
- **Front end:**
  - Each claim row has a user entry (`claim-review-user`), an "Assign review" button (`claim-review-assign`) and the assigned user (`claim-review-assigned`). A refusal shows the row's `claim-error`.
  - The header has a "My reviews" counter (`my-reviews-count`): the number of REVIEW claims assigned to the signed-in user.

Two behaviours you might not assume:
- **The assignment stays after review.** Once a claim is reviewed and goes back to OPEN, its row still shows the assigned user. The header count stops including it, because it only counts claims still in REVIEW.
- **Any steward can review an assigned claim,** not just the assigned user. The test does exactly this, so I didn't restrict it.
